<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **40** documentable anchor(s).

**27** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f45c0125143c766d1d7900590747ad8acded344e`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `sys_user (literal, 52 pages)`
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **177** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f45c0125143c766d1d7900590747ad8acded344e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `73af106cfd0c4bd6b271bd44f649f2f40dce0296` — the merge of head `f183d45b4b3e3313f951dcaddb9b13931a95bf1f` into base `f45c0125143c766d1d7900590747ad8acded344e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 73af106cfd0c4bd6b271bd44f649f2f40dce0296 && git checkout 73af106cfd0c4bd6b271bd44f649f2f40dce0296
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f45c0125143c766d1d7900590747ad8acded344e f183d45b4b3e3313f951dcaddb9b13931a95bf1f && git checkout -B drift-repro f45c0125143c766d1d7900590747ad8acded344e && git merge --no-ff f183d45b4b3e3313f951dcaddb9b13931a95bf1f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f45c0125143c766d1d7900590747ad8acded344e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f45c0125143c766d1d7900590747ad8acded344e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f3393c48d56fa622962c68ad47175cc00c13810e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/auth-config.zod.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-only-local-password.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-user-endpoints.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-before-hook.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-auth-instance.ts

PR #33177 (draft), card #32087 item 5, judged against ruling record 6866334319 (item 5 → D), claim 6866387589 and its amendment 6866474074. Inputs: the card body and all 22 comments, the PR body and its 14-file list, the net diff against `main`, and the check-runs on this head. The remainder of the diff (three test files and one test stub, the changeset, `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`, the regenerated `content/docs/references/system/auth-config.mdx`) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`; the changeset is read here for ② only.

Check-runs on this head, read 2026-11-14T00:15Z: 26 success, 10 skipped, 29 in progress, 0 failed. Concluded green: Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, Lint & Repo Gates and every Lint shard, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Build Docs, PR-body guards, Dogfood Regression Gate. Not yet concluded: Build Core, Test Core 1–8 of 8, Test UI 1–16 of 16, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check UI, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI. The test and workspace type-check verdicts are therefore not in this record; the landing pre-check reads them.

### ① Derived judgments

1. `@objectstack/spec`, `AuthConfigSchema.ssoOnlyMode`: TSDoc and `.describe` text only. No key, value, type or export moves; the accept set is unchanged. Named right. The one generated artifact that carries the text is regenerated in the diff.
2. `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, accept set: with SSO-only mode on, four doors (`POST /set-initial-password`, `POST /admin/set-user-password`, `POST /reset-password`, `POST /phone-number/reset-password`) answer `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` to a request for a user whose `sys_user.source` is `idp_provisioned`, where on `main` they answer it. A deployment that already runs with `ssoOnlyMode` or `OS_AUTH_SSO_ONLY=true` meets the refusal on upgrade, with no configuration change. This is a narrowing of what the published package accepts. Named **wrong**: the PR body and the changeset say `Clause-②: no` with no arm. See ②.
3. `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, public surface: `AuthManager` gains the public method `isSsoOnlyMode()`, and the exported `AdminUserEndpointDeps` gains the optional member `ssoOnlyMode?()`. Both are additive on names the package index publishes. Not named anywhere in the PR body or the changeset. Named **wrong** by omission. See ②.
4. Error vocabulary: no code is minted. The set doors answer the nested ADR-0112 envelope with `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` / `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`; the reset doors answer the vendor's flat body with the same two codes. Named right.
5. `readUserSource` moves from `admin-user-endpoints.ts` to the new module with its engine passed in. It was module-private and stays off the package index. No surface change. Named right.
6. `Metadata-protocol: none`: no metadata an author writes changes shape. Named right, consistent with the earlier auth-door changesets.

### ② Semver level

- Level: `patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-auth` and `@objectstack/spec`. Right. A non-protocol change ships `patch` whether it widens or breaks (AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist step 3), and the spec half is description text.
- Clause-②: line: **wrong**, and this is the must-fix.
  - The diff publishes a narrowing (① item 2) and declares none. The repository's own stock is consistent on this class: `.changeset/32113-scim-identity-source.md` (the same door, `admin/set-user-password`, answering `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` to a newly covered population) declares `yes (narrowing)`; `.changeset/plugin-auth-second-factor-code-and-link-doors.md` and `.changeset/environment-membership-removal-next-request.md` (an existing door answering differently for a population, nothing re-shaped) declare `no (narrowing)`; the cloud-managed precedent the decision analysis cites (#25399) shipped as `fix(plugin-auth)!` with a BREAKING banner. The contract-review template states the same reading: a change that makes the spec's own refusal real is reviewed on the narrowing face.
  - The diff also widens the public surface (① item 3). `.changeset/auth-handlerequest-whole-surface.md` names new `AuthManager` methods as a widening and declares `yes (narrowing)` for the pair.
  - What the declaration owes, all on the prose faces and the PR's own metadata, no code: the line `Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — …` in the PR body and the changeset (or `no (narrowing)` if the seat rules the two additive members off the published accept set, with that ruling written down); `!` in the title; a BREAKING banner in the changeset that says who moves (a deployment already in SSO-only mode); exactly one ADR-0087 disposition marker; a `Skills-docs:` line (the diff does update `authentication.mdx`, so `updated here` or `none — REASON` is the seat's call); and the dogfood battery pinned to the head, which the dev report skipped as `n/a` on the strength of the missing arm.
- `What to do` in the changeset is accurate and stays.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev report 6868164456, `deviations`: (1) the card's newest `Claim:` line is the sibling item-4 claim; claim 6866387589 names this branch and its amendment names this surface, so the branch is covered. Answered. (2) no assignee or reviewer write through MCP. Answered. (3) one merge of `main` before opening, docs only. Answered.
- `open_questions`: empty.
- `security_findings`: `withheld`. It is not readable from this review's inputs and is not judged here. One item is with the security seat.
- `remainders`: the administrator's set-password warning (ui) and the governed ADR-0135 D5.2 note are both on the ruling's work list and carry no card number yet. The seat files them before ACCEPT. Until the governed note lands, ADR-0135 D5.2's second bullet (an SSO-onboarded user setting an initial password) reads wider than the code does under SSO-only mode; the spec text in this diff is the accurate one.
- The reading "the set and reset doors refuse an IdP-provisioned user who already holds a password": inside the ruling's first bullet (every door that gives a local password), and the ruling's third bullet is kept, since a password already held still signs in and still changes on `/change-password`. Answered. ADR-0135 D5.2's stamp narrows this case further: gaining a local credential makes the row read `env_native`, so a user who holds a local password normally meets no refusal at any of the four doors.
- PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no off-relay author to name. The PR is a draft.

### ④ Design judgment

Read in the live tree at this head: the four door sites, the shared judge, the platform-admin gate, the impersonation endpoint's target rule, the identity-source stamp, the phone-number plugin options, the existing reset-token reader, `cloud-managed.ts`, ADR-0135 D5.2; and the vendor's 1.7.12 source for `/reset-password`, `/phone-number/reset-password` and `resetCredentialPassword`.

**`packages/spec/src/system/auth-config.zod.ts`** — against ruling 6866334319 item 5 → D and its first consumer (`AuthManager.resolveSsoOnly`, read by the four doors). Sentence by sentence:
- "refuses to give an IdP-provisioned user (`sys_user.source = 'idp_provisioned'`) a local password at every door that sets one": holds. The four doors are the ones that write a password hash for an existing user without proof of the current one. `/change-password` proves the current one; sign-up is off under SSO-only; create-user and import write new rows only; SCIM writes no credential; the email-OTP reset is not in the plugin list; the vendor's own `/admin/set-user-password` is shadowed by the mount this diff edits, and `/admin/update-user` refuses a password key.
- "answer `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`": holds at all four.
- "One exception keeps break-glass: a platform administrator may set their own local password": holds, and is the ruling's exception. See nit 1 for the one population where the four doors do not agree.
- "Environment-native users are unaffected": holds; a row with no source is answered as before, as at the cloud-managed door.
- "a local password a user already holds keeps working (sign-in and change-password)": holds; no sign-in or change-password path is touched.
- SSO-only off: the judge returns before any read; holds.
The description holds against the ruling. No finding on this file beyond ②.

**`sso-only-local-password.ts`** — the rule and the judge agree with the header. `unreadable` fails closed as `503` at every door. The reset-door reader matches the vendor's handlers: same identifier strings, same token precedence (body, then query), same expiry comparison, same attempt-budget arithmetic and split, same user lookup by `phoneNumber`; the phone plugin is configured without a custom verifier and with the same `allowedAttempts` default the hook passes, so the stored-code reading is the door's own.

**`admin-user-endpoints.ts`** — the arm sits after the user-exists check and the cloud-managed arm and before the hash; nothing is written ahead of it. `actor.id === userId` behind `gateAdmin` is the exception as ruled: the gate admits platform administrators only, and the impersonation endpoint refuses a platform administrator as target, so the actor is the person. Another administrator as target is refused. Agrees.

**`auth-plugin.ts`** — the set-initial-password arm judges the session user with the cloud-managed door's own predicate; a caller with no session falls through to the body as before; `adminUserDeps` reads the switch live. Agrees.

**`auth-manager-before-hook.ts`** — the arm runs only for the two reset paths with the switch on, only for a user the reader names, and ahead of the complexity check. Agrees.

**`auth-manager.ts`, `auth-manager-auth-instance.ts`** — wiring only; `isSsoOnlyMode()` returns `resolveSsoOnly()`. Agrees.

Findings:

1. **must-fix** — ②: the `Clause-②:` declaration names neither the narrowing nor the widening this diff publishes, and the obligations that hang on the arm (the `!`, the BREAKING banner, the ADR-0087 marker, the `Skills-docs:` line, the dogfood battery) were not met. Fix on the prose faces and the PR title and body; the code does not move.
2. **nit** — the exception asks two predicates: the set doors read the session's `isPlatformAdminUser`, which also reads the legacy `role` scalar; the reset doors read `isPlatformAdminUserId`, the grant alone. A deployment that still carries only the legacy scalar is admitted at the set doors and refused at the reset doors. The stricter answer is the reset doors'; the module header names both predicates. Accepted deviation, or one sentence in the header.
3. **nit** — the prose faces say each door answers `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` and do not say that the reset doors answer the vendor's flat `{ code, message }` body while the set doors answer the nested envelope. One sentence in `authentication.mdx`.
4. **nit** — `/request-password-reset` and `/phone-number/request-password-reset` still send the mail or text to a user whose reset door will then answer 409. Not in the ruling; a follow-up card.
5. **nit** — the header's "not narrowed" list does not cite ADR-0135 D5.2's stamp (a row that gains a local credential reads `env_native`), which is what a reader needs to place the "already holds a password" case. One sentence in the header.

One item is with the security seat.

A must-fix stands, so the round does not end here: the fix earns a delta review by this reviewer. Because the fix is confined to the prose faces and the PR's title and body, ④ on the code above continues to cover the head it moves to.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f183d45b4b3e3313f951dcaddb9b13931a95bf1f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/auth-config.zod.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-only-local-password.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-user-endpoints.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-before-hook.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-auth-instance.ts

Delta round on PR #33177 (draft), card #32087 item 5, after record 6868317289 (FAIL at `f3393c48`). The verdict covers the whole PR at this head. Read this round: the delta `f3393c48..f183d45b` (3 commits, 6 files: the changeset, `authentication.mdx`, `sso-only-local-password.ts`, `auth-manager-before-hook.ts`, two test files), the rewritten PR title and body, the claim amendment 6869194964, and the check-runs on this head. `packages/spec/src/system/auth-config.zod.ts`, `admin-user-endpoints.ts`, `auth-plugin.ts`, `auth-manager.ts` and `auth-manager-auth-instance.ts` are byte-identical to the round-1 head; ④ for them is the round-1 reading. Ruling judged against: 6866334319 (item 5 → D).

Check-runs on this head, read 2026-11-14T01:26Z: 27 success, 12 skipped, 30 in progress, 0 failed. Concluded green: Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness, every Lint shard, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Build Docs, Dogfood Regression Gate. Check Changeset concluded green on this head at 01:17Z and is running again after the title and body rewrite. Not yet concluded: that re-run, Build Core, Test Core 1–8 of 8, Test UI 1–16 of 16, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check UI, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI. The test and workspace type-check verdicts are not in this record; the landing pre-check reads them.

### ① Derived judgments

1. `@objectstack/spec`, `AuthConfigSchema.ssoOnlyMode`: description text only, untouched by the delta. Named right.
2. `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, accept set: with SSO-only mode on, the four local-password doors answer `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` to a user whose `sys_user.source` is `idp_provisioned`. Now named, in the PR body and the changeset, as a narrowing. Named right.
3. New in the delta, same accept set: with SSO-only mode on, the two reset doors answer `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` when the reset record, or the user it names, cannot be read. Named in the same `Clause-②:` line. Named right.
4. `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, public surface: `AuthManager#isSsoOnlyMode()` and the optional `AdminUserEndpointDeps.ssoOnlyMode?()`. Now named as the widening. Named right.
5. The delta changes the return type of `resolveResetDoorUserId` and adds `SSO_ONLY_RESET_UNREADABLE_MESSAGE` and `ResetDoorSubject`. The module is not on the package index, so nothing published moves. Named right by silence.
6. Error vocabulary: no code is minted; the new answer uses the registered `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`. Named right.
7. `Metadata-protocol: none`. Named right.

### ② Semver level

- Level: `patch` on both packages. Right; a non-protocol change ships `patch` and keeps its banner and disposition.
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`: right. The line is byte-identical in the PR body and the changeset (the three declaration lines compared), and the claim amendment 6869194964 carries the same value.
- `!` is in the PR title and in the changeset's summary line.
- The changeset carries a `**BREAKING**` paragraph that says who moves (a deployment already running with SSO-only mode on) and what they do.
- Exactly one ADR-0087 marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, with a reason that matches the diff: no key, value or type moves and nothing stored is rewritten.
- `Skills-docs: none — …`: holds. Nothing under `skills/**` names SSO-only mode or these doors, and the diff itself adds the rule to `authentication.mdx`.
- Dogfood: the per-PR CI run does not carry the dogfood shards by design (they run on the queue build), so the evidence on a PR head is the dev's battery. The PR body reports it full and green (462 files passed, 3 skipped; 3905 tests passed, 42 skipped; exit 0) on `10afe71b`. The head differs from that commit by six docblock lines in `sso-only-local-password.ts` and nothing else, so the reading covers this head. The seat's pre-queue check reads the same line.

The round-1 must-fix is closed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- PR body, acceptance notes: nits 2, 3 and 5 taken as prose; nit 4 left for the seat. Answered; nit 4 stays a follow-up card for the seat to file.
- `remainders` (the administrator's set-password warning, the governed ADR-0135 D5.2 note): unchanged from round 1, still without card numbers. The seat files them before ACCEPT.
- Round-1 dev report `security_findings: withheld`: not readable from this review's inputs and not judged here.
- The item round 1 left with the security seat is addressed in this delta and judged in ④ below. No item is left with the security seat from this review.
- PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`. The PR is a draft.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/system/auth-config.zod.ts`** — unchanged; the round-1 sentence-by-sentence reading stands. The description says nothing about the new 503 arm, and does not need to: it states the rule and its exception, and the fail-closed answer is a property of two doors that the changeset and `authentication.mdx` state.

**`sso-only-local-password.ts`** (delta) —
- `resolveResetDoorUserId` now answers one of three: a user the presented credential names, nobody, or unreadable. Unreadable is answered when there is no verification read surface, when the verification read throws, when the texted code matches and there is no user read surface, and when the user lookup throws. A path that is not a reset door answers nobody before anything is read. Every arm that answered nobody in round 1 for a credential the door would itself refuse still answers nobody, so those requests are answered exactly as before; the comparisons against the vendor's handlers (identifier strings, token precedence, expiry, attempt budget, user lookup) are unchanged.
- The header now names the predicate each door asks and where the two differ (nit 2), and cites ADR-0135 D5.2's stamp (nit 5). Both paragraphs agree with `platform-admin-gate.ts`, `AuthManager#isPlatformAdminUserId` and `stampIdentitySource` as read in round 1.

**`auth-manager-before-hook.ts`** (delta) — the arm starts from `unreadable` when the reader could not read, judges the named user when there is one, and otherwise allows. `refuse` answers 409 as before; `unreadable`, from either the reader or the source read, answers 503 with one message, ahead of the vendor's handler, so nothing is written. The arm still runs only for the two reset paths with the switch on. Agrees with the header and with the changeset.

**Pins** (lane seat's ACCEPT; read for the fix only) — the module pin covers the four unreadable cases and that another path reads nothing; each reset door has a leg, on the real engine, that makes the verification reads throw and asserts 503, the code, the message and no credential row. The PR body reports the ablation of the reader's unreadable answer turning exactly these three red.

**`admin-user-endpoints.ts`, `auth-plugin.ts`, `auth-manager.ts`, `auth-manager-auth-instance.ts`** — unchanged; round-1 reading stands.

**`authentication.mdx`, changeset** (prose) — the fail-closed sentence and the body-shape bullet (nit 3) agree with the code.

Nothing else in the delta moves the contract judged in round 1.

Findings:

1. **nit** (carried from round 1, nit 4) — `/request-password-reset` and `/phone-number/request-password-reset` still send the mail or text to a user whose reset door will then answer 409. Not in the ruling; a follow-up card for the seat.

Round-1 findings 1 (must-fix), 2, 3 and 5 are closed. Nits alone remain, so the round ends here.

**ACCEPT · 2026-11-14T01:46Z · PR #33177 · head `f183d45b`**

1. **Shape:** `Part of #32087` (item 5, server half), base `main`, 14 files (+1133/−35): one shared SSO-only judge in plugin-auth beside the cloud-managed one, wired into the four local-password doors; the `ssoOnlyMode` description in `packages/spec` and its generated reference; `authentication.mdx`; tests; one changeset (`@objectstack/plugin-auth` and `@objectstack/spec`, patch, `!`). `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, matching claim 6866387589 as amended by 6866474074 and 6869194964. Assignee `os-tesla`. Author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.
2. **Premise:** ruling 6866334319, item 5 → D. With SSO-only on, every door that gives a local password refuses an IdP-provisioned user, except a platform administrator's own break-glass password. A password already held keeps working. With SSO-only off, nothing changes.
3. **Contract review:** owed at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` (a published schema description). Round 1 was FAIL 6868317289 on the declaration. The delta review is PASS 6869357395 on this head and covers the whole PR. Its one open nit (the request-reset doors still send a code to a user whose reset will be refused) is a follow-up outside the ruling, in the seat hand-over.
